scope: H5 open-arena DCM-control effect primitive only
scientific_role: mechanism-definition decision; not parameter fitting, ranking, or promotion evidence

decision.rule: H5-v1 may alter only the conditional post-reorientation direction distribution at ordinary H3-null reorientation event times.
decision.event_timing_rule: H5-v1 may not alter the baseline mean free path, reorientation hazard, event threshold process, or event timing.
decision.baseline_mean_free_path_role: A shared baseline mean_free_path_mm may remain a nuisance parameter of the H3-null locomotion substrate, but H5 biology may not make it depend on recent history, origin-relative heading, radial position, or treatment.

Bonavita_et_al_2026.finding: In origin-referenced analyses of Lasius niger, both turning-angle distributions and mean free-path distributions depended on heading relative to the starting point; free paths were shorter when moving away from the start than when moving toward it.
Bonavita_et_al_2026.importance: This is genuine biological support for an orientation-dependent free-path mechanism class.
Bonavita_et_al_2026.scope_limit: Those data come from a different release/search experiment. The effect magnitude is not an independently validated H5 parameter for the Poissonnier assay.
Bonavita_et_al_2026.decision_interpretation: The free-path finding is deferred, not rejected as biology. It is excluded from H5-v1 because the current Poissonnier development targets cannot separately identify it from the direction-steering primitive.

simulator_mapping.H3_null_relation: In the audited H3 continuous-time substrate, hazard = speed / mean_free_path_mm. Therefore an orientation-dependent free-path rule is mathematically an orientation-dependent reorientation-hazard rule.
simulator_mapping.consequence: Adding free-path modulation would give H5 two coupled effect axes: conditional direction and event timing.
simulator_mapping.distinction_from_failed_H3: This would not be identical to failed H3-v1 because the hazard would depend on origin-relative heading rather than only travel history, but it would reopen the event-timing mechanism axis that H5 was designed to keep separate.

stress_audit.diagnostic_implementation: A temporary working-tree-only H3 hook was installed inside the CI runner, exercised, then restored before artifact upload. git diff --exit-code and H3/RNG/firewall regressions proved the audited runtime was restored exactly.

identifiability_reasoning.aggregate_target_limit: The frozen development objective contains time_to_exit_s, middle_zone_fraction, beeline_mm, and exit_edge only. It contains no origin-conditioned segment-length or event-hazard observable.
identifiability_reasoning.stress_result: Direction-only and free-path-only perturbations move the aggregate observables in substantially aligned directions over multiple strengths and under isotropic entry headings.
identifiability_reasoning.combined_result: At low/mid engineering strengths the combined perturbation is almost collinear with the sum of the two individual perturbations, showing that a two-axis model can trade one primitive against the other while producing similar aggregate movement.
identifiability_reasoning.parameter_cost: Allowing free-path modulation would require at least one additional effect magnitude or a separately frozen external law while also changing event timing.
identifiability_reasoning.claim_rule: The current aggregate data cannot justify attributing a fitted H5 improvement separately to directional choice and free-path anisotropy.

parsimony_and_falsifiability.direction_only_reachability: Engineering-only tests show that changing conditional direction alone has substantial reachability on exit timing and trajectory geometry, so free-path modulation is not required merely to make H5 capable of moving the development observables.
parsimony_and_falsifiability.narrower_claim: H5-v1 tests one new biological primitive: history-modulated origin-referenced directional choice at otherwise baseline reorientation events.
parsimony_and_falsifiability.future_discriminator: Orientation-dependent free-path modulation should be reconsidered only with raw/segmented trajectory evidence, a separately justified transferable external law, or a new hypothesis version whose evaluation can directly distinguish event timing from turn direction.

next_step: Resolve the radial-gate form and whether its scale is fixed, simplified away, or estimated.
